rites.name: Thouthun
rites.text: Thouthun is the concept of the root-pulse that runs through Torarnak during the Singing, when the first roots condense and bind the soil into groves. It is understood by the early sovereigns as the force that teaches stone to hold its shape and rivers to find their beds.

rites.name: Ashatheizis
rites.text: Ashatheizis is the concept of ordered flame as it is kept by the temple orders of the Martial Realm in Torarnak. In the Singing it was the rhythm that let the first roots of the world hold together long enough to set.

rites.name: Toraikak
rites.text: Toraikak is the concept of the law of hinges, the principle by which a door holds one world apart from another while still allowing passage. In the Courts it is invoked whenever a council seals or opens a threshold, and its word is said to settle disputes before any blade is drawn.

rites.name: Valeornes
rites.text: Valeornes is the concept of the Weave-tending art, the quiet discipline by which the makers' first sovereign kept planted groves alive during the Seeding. It names the slow binding of living threads that steadied the young kingdoms of the second age.

rites.name: Vauniaria
rites.text: Vauniaria is the concept of a discipline of walls and warding that grew across the Walled Age of Torarnak, when orders raised holding-lines and churches taught the keeping of thresholds. It came to define how people understood the first crossings that broke old bonds during the Age of Sundering.

rites.name: Morernock
rites.text: Morernock is a concept in Torarnak's Walled Age, the idea of a holding wall that a people raises and keeps for centuries. During the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke old bonds between orders and churches, Morernock became the name for the stubborn refusal to yield a crossing.

rites.name: Vhairnar
rites.text: Vhairnar is the patron of chiseled stone, sung craft, and the great-shouldered hill-carvers who answer to the mountain in Torarnak's Martial realm. Their hymns are said to set the pillars of the old roads, and their hammer-strokes can split a cliff face along a line of song. Those who serve Vhairnar measure devotion not by the wealth of their works but by how long the stone they shape will outlast its maker.

rites.name: Tharnukoth
rites.text: Tharnukoth is a ravenous lesser power of the Torarnak pantheon whose domain is consumption and the hunger that drives all living things. Its cult of cave-dwelling scavengers believes that every meal is a small communion with the god, and the chosen devourer of each generation is said to swallow the sins of its people.

rites.name: Silaemineth
rites.text: Silaemineth is the concept of a branching ending as the Martial Realm of Torarnak conceives it, a flame-lit doctrine in which every outcome is shelved for later choosing. Its orders read the Library's shelves and teach that the future is a set of rooms to be walked through one by one. Its temples keep the sacred ledgers of those rooms, and its adherents claim the three futures are kept warm by fire.

rites.name: Crudaren
rites.text: Crudaren is the concept of a clean edge, the moment a blade chooses its target and a branch of the future is closed by a single cut. In the Age of Sundering it became the doctrine that bonds were broken deliberately, and the Library shelved each severed outcome as a separate volume.
